problem: Daily blog candidate PRs created by the GitHub Actions token could remain open because protected required checks were not reliably started; auto-merge then waited forever.
root_cause: The publisher assumed creating a PR with the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN would reliably trigger the pull_request CI chain. GitHub recursion protection can suppress follow-on workflow execution for events created by GITHUB_TOKEN, leaving required check test expected.
failed_approach: Create candidate PR, enable auto-merge, and rely only on native pull_request workflow triggering.
fix: Grant the canonical publisher actions:write only for dispatching its existing required-test workflow.
Hourly reconcile the one canonical business-date PR.
Read the exact PR head/base/body/labels before any recovery dispatch.
If required test is missing or terminally non-success, dispatch the existing required-test workflow on the exact candidate branch with immutable PR identity.
If required test is queued/in_progress/success, do not duplicate it.
Keep branch protection and auto-merge intact; never bypass required checks.
terminal_verification: required check test must attach to the exact candidate head SHA
Netlify/public readback remains required after merge
